next_experiment.reason: The domain check is INCONCLUSIVE only because R2 is statistically unreliable (Cd drift_rel -0.02625, Cd uncertainty 0.02625, St uncertainty 0.019654). R2's window start (107.29) is an MSER cap, so the transient may not have ended. Extending R2 is the only way to get a certified R0 vs R2 domain comparison. Two experiments remain, and this one plus REDUCE_TIME_STEP on R0 closes both open components. I run the domain experiment first because it is the less certain to resolve and may still expose a change above tolerance.
next_experiment.expected_outcome: R2's window moves past the transient, with drift_rel and the Cd and St uncertainties at or below 0.015. The verifier can then compute the domain component from R0 vs R2. If the stationary Cd and St stay within about 1.5% of R0 (Cd 1.3306, St 0.16318), the domain is within budget. A change above 3% beyond 2x noise would be a deterministic FAIL and R0 would be rejected.

reasoning_summary: Deterministic verdict is INCONCLUSIVE with failed_checks empty. I can't ACCEPT, because the time and domain components are INCONCLUSIVE for both Cd and St. I can't REJECT, because no FAIL was measured.

Mesh is certified for both quantities. Cd mesh uncertainty is 0.00761 and St mesh uncertainty is 0.0118 (three-level Celik, observed p=3.01). R0 (Cd 1.3306, St 0.16318) to R4 (Cd 1.334, St 0.16454) changes by 0.254% for Cd and 0.828% for St.

R0 statistics and averaging are fine: 11 cycles, Cd CI95 0.00097218, statistics uncertainty 0.002267 (Cd) and 0.002498 (St), averaging bias 0.0004734 (Cd) and 0.000352 (St). RUN_LONGER on R0 would add little.

R5 (R2 run to 430 convective units) is now statistically reliable. It has 40 cycles, Cd CI95 0.0002689 and drift_rel 0.0017393. Its stationary window values are Cd 1.3216 and St 0.16254, against R0's Cd 1.3306 and St 0.16318. The demonstrated change is 0.68% for Cd and 0.39% for St, far below the 0.03 tolerance. No domain FAIL is indicated.

The domain check is still INCONCLUSIVE. With only two levels (R0, R5) the verifier assumes order p=1 with Fs=3, which gives 0.04075 (Cd) and 0.02349 (St). Both exceed the 0.015 half-tolerance budget. This is a conservative extrapolation, not a measured error.

R1, R2 and R5 have checkMesh_ok false and a coarser far-field mesh than R0 (representative size 0.79405 D vs 0.45745 D, wake_last_cell_D 1.9729 vs 1.0209). The domain comparison is therefore slightly confounded with mesh.

A third domain level would probably not give a usable result with one experiment left. R1, from R0, was run only to 80 convective units and was unreliable (drift_rel 0.27794). R5 needed a stationary window starting at 180.58 in the larger domain. An EXPAND_DOMAIN child of R5 would likely hit the same transient problem.

The time component is still unmeasured: no REDUCE_TIME_STEP run exists. R0 uses dt 0.01 convective units, max Courant 0.7323 and 612.82 steps per period. R3 and R4, also children of R0, were reliable at 80 units (Cd CI95 2.576e-05 and 1.7905e-05). A time-step child of R0 should therefore give a clean, same-domain time estimate for about 2116 s.

Budget: 5 of 6 experiments used and 7.91 of 12.0 compute. One experiment remains. It can close the time component but not the domain component. The final outcome will likely be INCONCLUSIVE, unless the time-step run exposes a change above tolerance. That would be a FAIL.

All runs record a non-uniform inlet: ux_min 0.1125, ux_max 0.1875, mean 0.15, ux_nonuniformity 0.5. The question specifies a uniform stream. No menu primitive can measure or remove this and the verifier has no check for it. It is not a FAIL, but it is an unquantified risk and must be flagged to the submitter.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Temporal error at dt 0.01 convective units (backward scheme, max Courant 0.7323) is negligible, well below 1.5% for Cd and St.
hypotheses.test: REDUCE_TIME_STEP on R0 with factor 2. If stationary Cd and St stay within about 1.5% of R0 (Cd 1.3306, St 0.16318) with reliable statistics, the time component passes. A change above 3% beyond 2x noise would be a deterministic FAIL.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Domain error is small. R5 vs R0 shows 0.68% (Cd) and 0.39% (St). The 4.07% and 2.35% verifier estimates come from the assumed p=1 with Fs=3 and are conservative.
hypotheses.test: Would need a third, reliable domain level with a long record. This is not affordable within the remaining single experiment.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The non-uniform inlet (ux 0.1125 to 0.1875) biases Cd and St independently of mesh, time step and domain.
hypotheses.test: No menu primitive can test this. Flag it to the submitter for an inlet-profile check.

next_experiment.reason: The time component is unmeasured for both quantities, and it is the only open component that one experiment can close cleanly. R0's same-domain, same-mesh children (R3, R4) ran reliably at 80 units, so a time-step child of R0 should be reliable. Domain refinement would likely give an unreliable short run in a larger domain, as R1 did. The cost is about 2116 s, which fits the remaining compute budget (7.91 of 12.0 used).
next_experiment.expected_outcome: If stationary Cd and St change by less than about 1.5% relative to R0 (Cd 1.3306, St 0.16318), the time component is within budget. The verdict will likely stay INCONCLUSIVE because of the domain component. If they change by more than 3% beyond 2x noise, that is a deterministic FAIL and R0 is rejected.
